summary:
What if we could understand the future of our land before building on it?

Our project, ARD (أرض), is an interactive web application designed to address the NASA Space Apps Challenge prompt “Be an Earth System Trend Detective” by helping users make smarter and more sustainable construction decisions in Kuwait. The app integrates NASA Earth observation data, historical environmental analysis, and future climate projections to help homeowners, architects, developers, and public authorities understand land conditions before building. By selecting a location on an interactive map, users can explore environmental changes, temperature and rainfall trends, potential environmental risks, and climate-responsive building recommendations. The app also features a Smart Home Design tool and an Urban Planning Studio, allowing users to explore sustainable solutions such as solar energy, natural ventilation, shading, and green spaces. This project is important because it promotes climate-aware construction, environmental sustainability, and long-term urban resilience while supporting the goals of Kuwait Vision 2035. By transforming complex Earth science data into accessible insights, ARD empowers individuals and authorities to make informed decisions and build communities prepared for future environmental challenges.
details:
ARD (أرض) is an interactive web application that combines NASA Earth observation data, historical environmental analysis, and future climate projections to help users make smarter and more sustainable construction decisions in Kuwait. Designed for homeowners, architects, developers, and public authorities, the platform allows users to select a location and explore its environmental history, temperature and rainfall trends, potential environmental risks, and future climate conditions. The app features two main experiences: a Homeowner Portal that provides climate-responsive building recommendations and a Smart Home Design tool, and an Urban Planning Portal that helps authorities explore sustainable solutions such as solar energy, green spaces, shaded walkways, and improved drainage systems.

How does it work?

The app uses NASA Earth observation resources and climate datasets, including NASA POWER, Earthdata, and climate projections, to investigate environmental changes in selected locations. Users begin by choosing a location on an interactive map, where the platform presents environmental information through visual dashboards, historical trend graphs, and easy-to-understand reports. The Land History Explorer helps users understand how environmental conditions have changed over time, while the Climate Trend Analysis feature explores historical patterns and possible future climate scenarios. Based on the available findings, the app provides general recommendations for sustainable building designs and environmental planning. Homeowners can explore conceptual house designs suited to local climate conditions, while urban planners can investigate environmental changes and explore sustainable development interventions. The interface is designed to make complex scientific information accessible and useful for everyday decisions.

What benefits does it have?

  • Informed Construction Decisions: Helps homeowners, architects, and developers understand environmental conditions before purchasing land or beginning construction.
  • Climate Resilience: Encourages building designs that consider changing temperatures, rainfall patterns, and potential future environmental challenges.
  • Environmental Awareness: Raises awareness of how land conditions and climate patterns change over time through accessible NASA Earth observation data.
  • Sustainable Architecture: Promotes climate-responsive design approaches such as natural ventilation, shading, solar energy, and green spaces.
  • Environmental Risk Awareness: Highlights potential environmental concerns and areas that may require further professional investigation before development.
  • Smarter Urban Planning: Supports developers and public authorities in exploring sustainable infrastructure, green corridors, and environmentally responsible neighborhood development.
  • Data Accessibility: Transforms complex scientific datasets into understandable maps, graphs, reports, and practical recommendations.
  • Supporting Kuwait Vision 2035: Aligns with Kuwait's goals of sustainable living environments, improved infrastructure, technological innovation, and long-term development.

What do you hope to achieve?

We aim to empower individuals, architects, developers, and public authorities to make more informed construction decisions by understanding the environmental history and possible future climate conditions of the land they plan to develop. By making NASA Earth observation data accessible and connecting it with sustainable architectural recommendations, ARD encourages climate-conscious construction, environmental awareness, and long-term planning. Starting in Kuwait, we hope to contribute to Kuwait Vision 2035 by promoting sustainable infrastructure, climate-resilient communities, and smarter urban development. On a larger scale, we envision expanding ARD beyond Kuwait, helping communities around the world use Earth science to create safer, more sustainable environments for future generations.

*What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?*

• *Frontend & Backend:* Google AI Studio

• *APIs:* Climate Data Online (CDO) & Meteomatics Weather API for fetching data that was given by NASA's Resources & Google Maps for Maps Integration.

• *Video Editing:* Capcut

• *Graphic Designing:* Canva

Don't just build for today's environment. Build for tomorrow's Earth.
